members.name: Edda Wray
members.role: keeper of the north light; Thornby says she lit it wrong to wreck boats
ties: accused by Osric Dunn of wrecking his brother's boat
grandmother of the boy who lives with her

members.name: Colm Wray
members.role: Edda's grandson, raised at the light; trims the wick, hauls water and keeps the oil jars
ties: plays with Wren Stave and Hob Dunn when Thornby folk come up the cape
afraid of the dark stair below the light
SECRET: saw his grandmother's light burn low one night last winter and has told no one

situations.summary: Thornby holds Edda's light to blame for the wreck that drowned Osric Dunn's brother, and Cuthbert Stave's brother's boat besides; Edda says she lights it every night and will not be driven off the cape. Colm has seen the light fail once and says nothing.

sides.Edda Wray: She keeps the light as her mother did, and she is tired of being called a wrecker by folk who never climbed the cape in a gale; she will not leave, and she will not beg.
sides.Osric Dunn: He buried his brother after that wreck and the village still owes Brackenford for the grain that followed; he wants Edda gone from the cape and says so at the cook-fire.
sides.Cuthbert Stave: His brother's boat came apart on the rocks below the light; he does not know if it was the light or the weather, and that not knowing has soured him.
sides.Colm Wray: He loves his grandmother and the light, and he is frightened by what he saw the night it burned low; he does not know who to tell or what it would mean.

situations.summary: The light burns oil the cape does not make; Edda trades smoked fish to Simon Hollis for lamp oil and salt, and this winter her store is short. Thornby's fisherfolk have quietly stopped selling her oil.

sides.Edda Wray: She needs oil before the cold sets in and will not ask Thornby for it; she would rather trade the last of her smoked fish than owe the village a favour.
sides.Simon Hollis: He carries her oil up the cape road and brings her fish down; he thinks Thornby is being hard on an old woman, but he will not say so at the gate.
sides.Tern Gannet: She packs smoked fish for the Brackenford market and has stopped buying Edda's; she blames the light for the near wreck last winter and will not put a mark in a wrecker's hand.
